key_insight: Peridynamic thermo-mechanical simulations predict cracking thresholds in tungsten under cyclic, fusion-relevant heat fluxes across different base temperatures.
engineering_relevance: The approach offers a pathway to screen plasma-facing materials and assess heat-flux-driven damage that limits fusion-component lifetime.
method: Run component-scale thermo-mechanical fracture simulations using CabanaPD.
Model cyclic electron-beam exposure across base temperatures and heat fluxes.
Track the spatial distribution and temporal accumulation of cracks and damage.
evidence_signal: Simulations informed by JUDITH electron-beam experiments on recrystallized pure tungsten agree well with experimental damage classifications.
watch_item: Validation described in the abstract concerns electron-beam-induced thermal damage, not the combined particle and neutron exposure of a fusion reactor.
paper_title: Peridynamic Thermo-Mechanical Modeling of Cracking in Tungsten under Fusion-Relevant Heat Fluxes
